proposed.why: Out of tool calls. The evidence shows one duplicated provider event that the ledger booked twice; I could not determine why the duplicate was produced, and recent_deploys failed twice.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The alert is real. evt_000272 (payment.succeeded, pay_000247, $104.44) reached Kafka twice: webhook-receiver queued it at partition 1 offsets 123 and 124, about 0.5 s apart, under two different trace ids. That pattern fits a provider webhook retry that the receiver did not deduplicate. ledger-consumer booked both copies as transactions 272 and 275, so the ledger is $104.44 ahead of the provider's records. The ledger dedupe works elsewhere: the metric shows 21 already_processed outcomes in the last 120 minutes. So the miss looks like a race between the two near-simultaneous copies, not a general failure. The trigger is not established. I could not check deploy or handler settings, because recent_deploys failed twice with a Docker timeout. I also did not check whether payment-confirmer handled the duplicate correctly. The other money-check invariants pass: the ledger balances, and our payments and refunds match the provider. The only damage is this one double-booked entry.

evidence.shows: Money check failed 2 of 5 invariants. evt_000272 was posted twice (transactions 272 and 275), and pay_000247 shows ledger $208.88 against provider $104.44, off by +$104.44. The ledger stays balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000272 twice, from provider-events/1@123 and 1@124, about 0.7 s apart, each in a different trace.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000272 twice, at offsets 123 and 124 on partition 1, 0.5 s apart, under two trace ids. The duplicate entered Kafka at the receiver.
Over 120 minutes the ledger recorded 21.25 already_processed outcomes against 483 posted, so its dedupe works in general.
No already_processed log lines in 120 minutes, although the metric counts them. The logs and the metric disagree, which I could not resolve.
The 5-minute series returned a single point, so it does not show when dedupe may have stopped working. It gives no evidence on timing.
recent_deploys failed with a Docker timeout, so no deploy or handler setting could be checked. A change in LEDGER_HANDLER cannot be ruled in or out. The same error came back at c5.

proposed_fix.summary: Reverse the duplicate ledger transaction 275 for evt_000272 with a compensating entry, so pay_000247 reads $104.44 and matches the provider. Then find why the duplicate event got past the receiver and the ledger dedupe. Once docker answers, rerun recent_deploys to check for a handler or deploy change, and make the ledger's dedupe on event_id atomic, for example with a unique constraint. Do not roll back yet: no deploy has been shown to be the cause, and a rollback repairs nothing already booked.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The repair touches one ledger transaction for one synthetic payment. A wrong reversal could unbalance the ledger or hide a real second charge, so confirm with the provider's records first. Adding a unique constraint could make the consumer fail on any other existing duplicates.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Delete the compensating entry to restore the prior state (the ledger would then be +$104.44 again). Take a snapshot of the ledger tables before the repair. Run money_check again afterwards to confirm that all five invariants pass.
